points.description: Gives two valid, distinct lists with fully valid reasoning: (1, 7, 103, 105) and (3, 5, 101, 107). Reasoning: s1=a1+a2=8, s2=a1+a3=104, s6=a3+a4=208, s5=a2+a4=112; s3,s4 are a1+a4 and a2+a3 in either order (106/110 or 110/106), giving the two lists. Equivalent methods are accepted, but both lists must be correct and no step may be invalid.

rubric.notes: Full mark only if two correct distinct lists are given with no invalid step. Any wrong step or wrong list earns 0. No partial credit.
rubric.answer_key:
Smallest sum is a1+a2=8, next is a1+a3=104, largest is a3+a4=208, second largest is a2+a4=112. The remaining sums 106 and 110 are a1+a4 and a2+a3 in some order.
Case 1: a1+a4=106, a2+a3=110. Since a3−a2=104−8=96, a3=103, a2=7, a1=1, a4=105. List (1,7,103,105). Check sums: 8,104,106,110,112,208.
Case 2: a1+a4=110, a2+a3=106. a3−a2=96, so a3=101, a2=5, a1=3, a4=107. List (3,5,101,107). Check sums: 8,104,110,106,112,208, which sort to 8,104,106,110,112,208.
